title: Homily I — She found grace and answered the angel

edition.locus: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), Homily I on the Dormition, col. 709 (PDF leaf 396)

source_text: Ὄντως εὗρε χάριν, ἡ ἀξία τῆς χάριτος. Εὗρε χάριν ἡ τοὺς πόνους τῆς χάριτος γεωργήσασα, καὶ πολὺ δρεψαμένη τὸν ἄσταχυν. Εὗρε χάριν, ἡ τοὺς σπόρους τῆς χάριτος γεννήσασα, καὶ πολύχουν δρεψαμένη τὸν ἄσταχυν τῆς χάριτος. Εὗρε χάριτος ἄβυσσον, ἡ σῶαν τὴν ὁλκάδα τῆς διπλῆς παρθενίας τηρήσασα, καὶ τὴν ψυχὴν γὰρ παρθένον ἐτήρησεν, οὐ τοῦ σώματος ἔλαττον. Ὅθεν καὶ ἡ τοῦ σώματος παρθενία τετήρητο. Καὶ τέξῃ, φησὶν, υἱὸν, καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν· Ἰησοῦς δὲ σωτὴρ ἑρμηνεύεται· αὐτὸς γὰρ σώσει τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ἐκ τῶν ἀνομιῶν αὐτῶν. Τί πρὸς ταῦτα τῆς ἀληθοῦς σοφίας ὁ θησαυρός, τὴν μὲν Εὔαν οὐ μιμεῖται τὴν προμήτορα, ἐπανορθοῦται δὲ μᾶλλον τὸ ταύτης ἀφύλακτον, καὶ συνήγορον τὴν φύσιν προβάλλεται, ὧδέ πως τῷ τοῦ ἀγγέλου ἀντιῤῥητορεύουσα ῥήματι· Πῶς ἔσται μοι τοῦτο, ἐπεὶ ἄνδρα οὐ γινώσκω; ἀδύνατα φθέγγῃ, φησίν. Ὁ γε σὸς λόγος τοὺς ὅρους λύει τῆς φύσεως, οὓς ὁ πλαστουργήσας ἐπήξατο. Οὐκ ἀνέχομαι Εὔα χρηματίσαι δευτέρα, καὶ τὸ τοῦ Ποιήσαντος παρακρούσασθαι βούλημα. Εἰ δὲ μὴ λέγεις ἀντίθεα, τὸν τρόπον εἰπὼν τῆς συλλήψεως, λῦσον τὴν ἀπορίαν. Πρὸς ἣν ὁ τῆς ἀληθείας ἄγγελος· Πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἐπελεύσεται ἐπὶ σὲ, καὶ δύναμις Ὑψίστου ἐπισκιάσει σοι. Διὸ καὶ τὸ γεννώμενον ἅγιον κληθήσεται Υἱὸς Θεοῦ. Οὐ δουλεύει φύσεως νόμοις τὸ τελούμενον. Ὁ γὰρ Δημιουργὸς καὶ δεσπότης τῆς φύσεως, κατ' ἐξουσίαν τοὺς ὅρους ἀμείβει τῆς φύσεως. Ἡ δὲ, τὸ ἀεὶ ποθούμενον καὶ τιμώμενον ὄνομα, μεθ' ἱερᾶς εὐλαβείας ἀκούσασα, τῆς ὑπακοῆς ἐπηφίει φόβου καὶ χαρᾶς γέμοντα ῥήματα, Ἰδοὺ ἡ δούλη Κυρίου, γένοιτό μοι κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου.
pass_a_gloss: Truly she found grace (εὗρε χάριν), the one worthy (ἀξία) of grace. She found grace who farmed (γεωργήσασα) the labours (πόνοι) of grace and plucked (δρεψαμένη) much the ear of grain (ἄσταχυς). She found grace who generated (γεννήσασα) the seeds (σπόροι) of grace and plucked the abundant-pouring (πολύχους) ear of grace. She found an abyss (ἄβυσσος) of grace, she who kept safe (σῶαν τηρήσασα) the merchant ship (ὁλκάς) of the double virginity; for she kept the soul virgin, not less than the body. Whence also the virginity of the body had been kept. And you will bear, he says, a son, and you will call his name Jesus; Jesus is interpreted saviour (σωτήρ); for he will save his people from their lawless deeds (ἀνομίαι). What to these things the treasure (θησαυρός) of true wisdom (σοφία)? She does not imitate (μιμεῖται) Eve the foremother (προμήτωρ), but rather corrects (ἐπανορθοῦται) her unguardedness (τὸ ἀφύλακτον), and puts forward nature as advocate (συνήγορος), thus somehow speaking against the word of the angel: How will this be to me, since I do not know a man? You utter impossible things, she says. Your word dissolves the boundaries (ὅροι) of nature, which the one who fashioned (πλαστουργήσας) fixed (ἐπήξατο). I do not endure (οὐκ ἀνέχομαι) to be named (χρηματίσαι) a second Eve, and to defraud the will (βούλημα) of the Maker. But if you do not speak things against God (ἀντίθεα), having told the manner (τρόπος) of the conception, resolve the perplexity (ἀπορία). To her the angel of truth: Holy Spirit will come upon you and power of the Most High will overshadow (ἐπισκιάσει) you; wherefore also the thing being born, holy, will be called Son of God. The thing being accomplished (τὸ τελούμενον) is not enslaved (οὐ δουλεύει) to laws of nature. For the Creator (Δημιουργός) and master (δεσπότης) of nature by authority (κατ' ἐξουσίαν) exchanges (ἀμείβει) the boundaries of nature. And she, the ever-longed-for and honoured name, having heard with holy reverence (εὐλάβεια), let go (ἐπηφίει) words of obedience (ὑπακοή) full of fear and joy: Behold the handmaid (δούλη) of the Lord; may it happen to me according to your word (ῥῆμα).
pass_b_english: Truly she found grace, she who was worthy of grace. She found grace who had tilled the labours of grace and reaped a rich harvest. She found grace who brought forth the seeds of grace and reaped the full-flowing harvest of grace. She found a depth of grace, she who kept safe and whole the ship of her twofold virginity: for she kept her soul a virgin no less than her body, and that is why the virginity of her body was also kept. “And you will bear a son,” he says, “and you shall call his name Jesus” (Luke 1:31). Jesus means Saviour, “for he will save his people from their iniquities” (Matthew 1:21).

And what does the treasure of true wisdom say to this? She does not imitate Eve, her first mother; rather, she sets right Eve's carelessness, and calls on nature as her advocate, arguing against the angel's word in some such way as this: “How will this be for me, since I do not know a man?” (Luke 1:34). “You speak of impossible things,” she says. “Your word breaks the boundaries of nature that the One who fashioned it set in place. I will not bear to be called a second Eve and to cheat the will of the Maker. But if what you say is not against God, tell me the manner of the conception and resolve my doubt.” To her the angel of truth replies: “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore the holy one to be born will be called the Son of God” (Luke 1:35). What is being done here is no slave to the laws of nature. For the Creator and Master of nature changes the boundaries of nature by his own authority. And she, hearing with holy reverence that name ever longed for and honoured, spoke words of obedience full of fear and joy: “Here is the servant of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word” (Luke 1:38).

choices.note: Edition note (99): R. reads εὗρες ('you found') throughout this run;
Edition note (1): Sangerm. lacks φησίν; no effect on the English.
Edition note (2): R. reads ἀντίθετα ('contradictions') for ἀντίθεα ('things against God');
γενόμενον judged wrong by the editor;
John's wording 'from their iniquities' (ἀνομιῶν) differs from Matthew 1:21 ('sins', ἁμαρτιῶν); the English keeps John's word.
The Eve contrast is a typological reference to Genesis 3, not a quotation; left uncited.
'τὸ ἀεὶ ποθούμενον καὶ τιμώμενον ὄνομα' is read as the object of ἀκούσασα (the name 'Son of God' just spoken); a neuter 'name' in apposition to the feminine 'she' is unlikely.
The 'ship' (ὁλκάς, a merchant vessel) image is kept.
'Behold' is rendered 'Here is' to avoid archaism.

notes: Edition note (99): R. reads εὗρες ('you found') throughout this run; English follows the printed εὗρε. Edition note (1): Sangerm. lacks φησίν; no effect on the English. Edition note (2): R. reads ἀντίθετα ('contradictions') for ἀντίθεα ('things against God'); English follows the printed text. Edition note (3): Germ. γενόμενον judged wrong by the editor; English follows γεννώμενον. John's wording 'from their iniquities' (ἀνομιῶν) differs from Matthew 1:21 ('sins', ἁμαρτιῶν); the English keeps John's word. The Eve contrast is a typological reference to Genesis 3, not a quotation; left uncited. 'τὸ ἀεὶ ποθούμενον καὶ τιμώμενον ὄνομα' is read as the object of ἀκούσασα (the name 'Son of God' just spoken); a neuter 'name' in apposition to the feminine 'she' is unlikely. The 'ship' (ὁλκάς, a merchant vessel) image is kept. 'Behold' is rendered 'Here is' to avoid archaism.
